name: Anguilla Residency by Investment (ARBI)

requirements.blocker_text: Minimum US$750,000 investment in qualifying real estate (home, villa, condominium, or hotel unit) for a family of up to 4; additional family members add US$100,000 each. Property is subject to a 5-year lock-in and cannot be resold within that period.
requirements.fix_path: Acquire qualifying Anguilla real estate at or above the required threshold.

requirements.blocker_text: Must pass due diligence screening. Fees (Full Program): processing US$3,000 (family)/US$500 (each additional member); due diligence US$7,500 (per adult)/US$3,000 (per child); permit US$20,000 (family)/US$5,000 (each additional member).
Minimum US$150,000 non-refundable contribution to Anguilla's Capital Development Fund, which finances public-sector projects and economic diversification.
requirements.fix_path: Make the required non-refundable contribution to the Capital Development Fund.

requirements.blocker_text: Must pass due diligence screening. Fee schedule for this track specifically was not broken out in the source reviewed (only the real estate track's fee schedule was itemised); a comparable processing/due-diligence/permit fee structure should be expected but is not confirmed here.

evidence_required.document: Proof of qualifying investment (real estate title/purchase agreement, or Capital Development Fund contribution receipt)

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: at least 9 months of residence per year, for 5 consecutive years, to qualify for British Overseas Territories Citizenship

sources.title: Government of Anguilla, Ministry of Finance -- Anguilla Residency by Investment (ARBI): real estate and Capital Development Fund investment options, eligibility, fees, and rights

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Anguilla's initial build. Confirmed at tier-1 via an official Ministry of Finance presentation document -- this corroborates what several tier-3 sources (Arton Capital, Residency Routes, and others) had described as 'two residency-by-investment programs', though only this tier-1 source is cited. Modelled as category 'settled' rather than 'business' because the program's own name and stated outcome is a grant of Permanent Residence, not an operating-business requirement -- this is a judgment call, flagged for review. leads_to_citizenship and citizenship_after_months (60 months) and the 9-months/year physical presence rule are stated explicitly in the source, not estimated. Residents 'receive the right to live without restrictions' but 'must obtain work permits and cannot vote' -- work_rights is therefore 'restricted', and voting rights are explicitly withheld regardless of duration held. A 'Tax Residency' investment option is mentioned in the source as a third track but its criteria are described as 'still being developed' -- not modelled as a requirement group since no defined rules exist yet to cite. A 'Phase 1 Retroactive Fast Track' with reduced fees and 30-day approval is also described, apparently for already-established/retroactive investors; this reads as a transitional or promotional phase rather than the standing program rules and was not modelled as a separate route -- flagged in case it is still active. Fee schedule detail is confirmed only for the real estate track; the Capital Development Fund track's own fee breakdown is not itemised in the source and is flagged as an open gap in the cdf_duediligence requirement above.
